highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.151.0 updates to Skia m151 and ports several hot-path conversions from native to managed C#.
highlights_body: This release focuses on interop and allocation overhead: color/premultiply conversions, HarfBuzzSharp tag parsing, and shaper glyph access all move to zero-copy or fully-managed code. It also fixes a native resource leak in SKImage.FromEncodedData and picks up several rounds of Chrome M151 upstream fixes.

bullets.detail: The bundled engine is bumped to Chrome milestone m151, plus multiple follow-up rounds of upstream m151 bug-fix merges.
Removes an unnecessary `unsafe` modifier requirement from GRContextOptions, simplifying consumer code that touches GPU context options.

bullets.lead: Native resource leak in SKImage.FromEncodedData(SKData, SKRectI)
bullets.detail: Fixes a native resource leak that occurred when decoding an image with an explicit subset rectangle.

bullets.lead: Hot-path conversions ported from native to managed C#
bullets.detail: SKColor→SKColorF conversion, single-value SKPMColor premultiply/unpremultiply, SKColor hex parsing, HarfBuzzSharp.Buffer.AddUtf8 and Tag.Parse, SKFourByteTag.Parse, and SKShaper glyph-result access are all reimplemented in managed code or as zero-copy spans, cutting P/Invoke and allocation overhead on these paths.

contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Managed color-conversion and premultiply ports, and Skia m151 sync work

preview_summaries.v4.151.0-rc.1.1: Release Candidate 1 added WASM Emscripten 5.0.6 static libraries for .NET 11 and merged further Chrome m151 bug fixes ahead of stable.
preview_summaries.v4.151.0-preview.2.1: Preview 2 ported HarfBuzzSharp.Buffer.AddUtf8 and Tag.Parse to allocation-free managed code and merged Chrome m151 bug fixes.
preview_summaries.v4.151.0-preview.1.1: Preview 1 updated Skia to milestone m151, ported SKColor/SKPMColor conversions to managed C#, and fixed the SKImage.FromEncodedData resource leak.

harfbuzz_summary: HarfBuzzSharp.Buffer.AddUtf8(string) becomes allocation-free via a pooled UTF-8 encode, and Tag.Parse drops a per-call char[4] allocation, alongside the bundled HarfBuzz refresh to 14.2.1.
